identity.description: A GLM whose linear terms are replaced by penalized SMOOTHS: y's link-mean = intercept + f1(x1) + ... + fp(xp), each f a spline whose wiggliness is penalty-controlled. Keeps the GLM's per-feature interpretability (each effect is a plottable 1-D curve) while capturing nonlinearity a straight coefficient cannot — the midpoint between GLM and black-box.

emits.note: link-mean prediction; pyGAM exposes native prediction_intervals from the smoothing basis (LinearGAM)
the smooths ARE spline-basis coefficients; exported per-term as partial-dependence curves with confidence bands — the plottable per-feature effect story

lam.note: the smoothing penalty — the model's single most important knob; lam -> inf collapses every smooth to a line (a plain GLM), lam -> 0 interpolates; pyGAM's gridsearch scans it natively

n_splines.note: basis size per term; sets the CEILING on wiggliness — lam does the actual regularizing

invariances.why: spline knots are placed by feature quantiles, so an affine rescale of a feature moves knots with the data and spans the same function space — the fit is unchanged

the second-derivative wiggliness penalty is NOT invariant under nonlinear reparameterization of x — a log-transform changes what counts as 'smooth' and hence the fit (though far less than for a strict linear model)
the penalized IRLS has no missing-value mechanism; rows must be complete
this driver's auto term-build treats every column as a numeric spline; pyGAM factor terms f() exist but need explicit term specs plus integer codes — off by default here

keeps the exponential-family assumption of the chosen class — Normal errors for LinearGAM, Bernoulli/logit for LogisticGAM, Poisson (equidispersion included) for PoissonGAM; additivity replaces LINEARITY, not the distribution
each smooth spends effective degrees of freedom the data must fund; at small n the penalty shrinks smooths toward lines gracefully, but many terms with few rows overfit

outside the boundary knots the spline basis has no data support — the boundary polynomial extends uncontrolled, so out-of-range predictions are not trustworthy (unlike a linear model's disciplined line)

featureStats.why: the spread between rank correlation (or mutual information) and Pearson correlation per feature — a monotone-but-curved or U-shaped relation is exactly the signal a smooth captures and a straight coefficient misrepresents
rows divided by candidate smooth terms bounds the edf budget the data can fund; a low ratio says shrink terms or raise lam before trusting any curve
the GAM analogue of collinearity — one feature's smooth expressible through another's makes the decomposition unidentifiable and the per-feature curves (the whole interpretability payoff) unreliable

modelMetrics.why: effective degrees of freedom of each fitted smooth — edf ~= 1 means the penalty collapsed the term to a line, the per-term commit-linear signal; large edf flags genuine curvature (or overfit if n is thin)
if the strictly-linear GLM matches the GAM's held-out deviance, the extra edf are not earning their keep — the family-internal simplicity gate
pyGAM's native generalized cross-validation objective for lam selection — the smoothing knob's honest scoreboard without a manual CV loop

edgeCases.condition: many smooth terms with small n
edgeCases.behavior: edf explosion; wiggly curves fit noise
edgeCases.note: raise lam / cut terms / fall back to GLM

edgeCases.condition: encoded categorical fed to a numeric spline term
edgeCases.behavior: nonsense smooth over arbitrary integer codes
edgeCases.note: route through factor terms or one-hot into linear terms
clamp inputs to the training range or warn
raise lam; drop one of the entangled features

edgeCases.condition: lam grid hits its search boundary
edgeCases.behavior: GCV optimum outside the scanned range

driver.constructor: LinearGAM(terms='auto', n_splines=..., spline_order=3, lam=...).gridsearch(X, y) — class picked by problem_type (LinearGAM/LogisticGAM/PoissonGAM)
driver.wrapperNeeds: EXTRA DEP: pygam is NOT in the sidecar's statsmodels stack — tranche T2 must add it to requirements (statsmodels.gam.api.GLMGam is the dep-free fallback at the cost of pyGAM's gridsearch/intervals). Adapter: class switch on problem_type; export per-term partial dependence + bands for the coefficients port

placementClaims.why: no native NaN handling; incomplete rows are lost from the penalized likelihood
the smooth itself absorbs monotone curvature — pre-transforming x is what the spline is FOR; only extreme-tail compression occasionally helps knot coverage
quantile-placed knots make the fit invariant to affine rescaling; standardization is wasted compute
categoricals cannot enter numeric spline terms; they must be encoded (and routed to linear/factor terms, not smooths)
